d: A name that holds a value.
h:
A variable is a name that holds a value. Variable values can be numbers, strings, booleans, data types, and more.

Name variables

Variable names can be any non-reserved string of letters, digits, and underscores that don't start with a digit.

LETTERS   -- valid
a1        -- valid
var_name  -- valid
_test     -- valid

if        -- NOT valid
25th      -- NOT valid

Variable names are case-sensitive, so TestVar and TESTVAR are different names. Avoid naming variables with an underscore and all uppercase letters, such as _VERSION, because Luau may reserve them for internal global variables.

Best practices

It's best practice to spell out words fully. Abbreviations generally make code easier to write, but harder to read. Following common naming practices when naming your variables can help you and others understand their meaning or purpose:

  • Use PascalCase names for class and enum-like objects.
  • Use PascalCase names for all Roblox APIs. camelCase APIs are mostly deprecated.
  • Use camelCase names for local variables, member values, and functions.
  • Use LOUD_SNAKE_CASE names for constants, such as const values or other values that you don't expect to change.
  • Don't capitalize entire acronyms within names. For example, write aJsonVariable or MakeHttpCall.

Reserved names

Luau reserves the following keywords, so you can't use them to name variables or functions:

  • and
  • for
  • or
  • break
  • function
  • repeat
  • do
  • if
  • return
  • else
  • in
  • then
  • elseif
  • local
  • true
  • end
  • nil
  • until
  • false
  • not
  • while

Assign values

To create a variable and assign a value to it, use the = operator. Put the variable on the left of the = and the value on the right. If you don't put a value, the value is nil.

Variables can have global or local scopes. They have global scope by default, but it's almost always better to create them with local scope because Luau accesses local variables faster than global ones. To give a variable local scope, put the keyword local before a variable's name when you assign a value to it. To give it local scope and also prevent reassigning it, use const instead of local. For more information, see Scope.

local nilVar
local x = 10
local word = "Hello"
local boolean = true

print(nilVar) -- nil
print(x) -- 10
print(word) -- Hello
print(boolean) -- true

Assign values to multiple variables

You can assign values to multiple variables in one line by separating each variable-value pair with a comma. If you have more variables than values, then Luau assigns nil to the extra variables. If you have more values than variables, Luau doesn't assign the extra values to any variables.

local a, b, c = 1, 2, 3
local d, e, f = 4, 5 -- extra variable
local g, h = 7, 8, 9 -- extra value

print(a, b, c) -- 1, 2, 3
print(d, e, f) -- 4, 5, nil
print(g, h) -- 7, 8

Change values

To change a value of a variable, assign another value to it.

local x, y = 10, 20
print(x) -- 10
print(y) -- 20

x = 1000
y = 2000
print(x) -- 1000
print(y) -- 2000

Const variables

To create a variable that you can't reassign, use const instead of local. Trying to reassign a const variable causes an error, including through a compound assignment operator such as +=.

const MAX_HEALTH = 100

MAX_HEALTH = 50 -- error: cannot reassign a const variable
MAX_HEALTH += 1 -- error: cannot reassign a const variable

Like local, const accepts a type annotation, such as const MAX_HEALTH: number = 100.

You can also declare a function with const, which prevents reassigning the name of the function.

const function addOneAndTwo()
    local result = 1 + 2
    print(result)
end

addOneAndTwo = nil -- error: cannot reassign a const variable

const makes the variable itself immutable, not the value that it holds. If a const variable holds a table, you can still change the contents of the table. To make the contents immutable as well, use table.freeze().

const SETTINGS = { volume = 0 }

SETTINGS.volume = 1 -- ok, changes a value inside the table
SETTINGS = {} -- error: cannot reassign a const variable

Unlike the keywords in Reserved names, const is contextual. Luau only treats it as a keyword where local is valid, so existing code that uses const as a variable name still works.

local const = 1
print(const) -- 1

const = 2 -- ok, `const` is a variable name here

For more information and edge cases, see the Luau documentation.

kid.simple: A variable is a name that holds a value, like `coins = 10`. You use variables to remember things in your game, such as scores, player names, or parts. This page explains how to name variables, give them values, change them, and lock them with `const` so they cannot change. Variables are one of the very first things every scripter learns.
kid.analogy: A variable is like a labeled jar. The label is the name, like "coins", and what is inside is the value, like 10. You can swap out what is inside whenever you want, unless the jar is sealed with `const`.
keyPoints: Make a variable with `local name = value`. Without a value, it starts as `nil`.
Names can use letters, digits, and underscores, but cannot start with a digit. `a1` works; `25th` does not.
Names are case-sensitive: `Score` and `score` are different variables.
You cannot use reserved words like `if`, `end`, `local`, or `function` as names.
Use `local` almost always. Local variables are faster than global ones.
Assign several at once: `local a, b = 1, 2`. Extra variables become `nil`; extra values are thrown away.
`const` makes a variable you cannot reassign, like `const MAX_HEALTH = 100`. The contents of a const table can still change.
Naming style: `camelCase` for normal variables, `PascalCase` for classes, and `LOUD_SNAKE_CASE` for constants.

terms.variable: A name that holds a value so you can use it later.
terms.value: The data stored in a variable, like `10`, `"Hello"`, or `true`.
terms.assign: To put a value into a variable using `=`.
terms.case-sensitive: Capital and lowercase letters count as different. `Coins` is not the same as `coins`.
terms.reserved word / keyword: A word Luau already uses for its own grammar, like `if`, `then`, or `end`. You cannot use it as a name.
terms.local: A keyword that limits where a variable can be used, to the block of code it was made in. Faster and safer.
terms.global: A variable made without `local`. Any code in the same script can use it, but it is slower.
terms.const: A keyword that makes a variable you cannot point at a new value after creating it.
terms.constant: A value that is not supposed to change, like the max health of 100.
terms.camelCase: Writing names with the first word lowercase and later words capitalized, like `playerScore`.
terms.LOUD_SNAKE_CASE: All capitals with underscores between words, like `MAX_HEALTH`.

example.title: Track a player's health
example.code:
const MAX_HEALTH = 100 -- cannot be reassigned

local playerName = "Nova"
local health = MAX_HEALTH
local isAlive = true

print(playerName, health, isAlive) --> Nova 100 true

-- Change a value
health = health - 30
print(health) --> 70

-- Assign several values at once
local x, y, z = 1, 2
print(x, y, z) --> 1 2 nil

-- MAX_HEALTH = 50 would cause an error because it is const
explain: `const MAX_HEALTH = 100` makes a value that the script cannot reassign.
`local` creates three variables holding a string, a number, and a boolean.
`health = health - 30` reads the old value, subtracts 30, and stores 70.
With three names but only two values, `z` gets `nil`.

watchOut: Forgetting `local`. The variable becomes global, which is slower and easier to mess up.
Typos in names. `Health` and `health` are two different variables.
Starting a name with a digit, like `1stPlace`. Use `firstPlace` instead.
Thinking `const` locks a table's contents. It only stops you reassigning the name; use `table.freeze` to lock contents.
Naming things with an underscore plus all caps, like `_VERSION`. Luau may reserve those.
